Documentation → Automation & Change Control → Mass Deploy

Mass Deploy

Push an approved template to one or many FortiWebs of the ADOM in one canary-gated job — an SMTP server change, an NTP or DNS change, a Web Protection Profile meant for some devices only — with secrets typed at deploy time and never stored.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsoperations.apply operations.template_apply operations.template_approve
📍 WhereFortiWeb ADOM → Operations → Automation → Mass Deploy (URL /web/mass-deploy/)
On this page
  • What is it?
  • What does it do?
  • Requirements
  • Permissions
  • How to use
  • Configuration

What is it?#

Mass Deploy pushes an approved template to one or many devices of the ADOM in a single job. Use it for a change that must land on many boxes at once: a new SMTP server, an NTP or DNS change, or a Web Protection Profile that only some devices should get.

It uses the same engine as Apply in the Template Library: the same dry-run preview, firmware check, per-device variables and canary-first background job.

What does it do?#

  • Lists the newest approved version of every template family of the ADOM.
  • Shows every device of the ADOM with its build, the template's fit on that build and its binding. A device bound to another version cannot be selected.
  • Asks for the template's secret fields (passwords, PSKs, private keys) at deploy time. A template never sends its own secret values.
  • Previews every push per device, then deploys: the first device is the canary, and the rest run only if it succeeds.
  • Keeps a history of every deploy made here, with the result per device.

Requirements#

  • A FortiWeb ADOM. The other device ADOMs draw the entry disabled: the bulk deploy writes FortiWeb configuration objects only. Global has no entry.
  • At least one approved template in the ADOM.

Permissions#

Action Needs
Open the page, preview and deploy operations.apply and operations.template_apply
Override a firmware refusal (with a reason) operations.template_approve

How to use#

  1. Open Operations → Automation → Mass Deploy.
  2. In Approved templates, click Select on the template.
  3. In Targets, tick the devices. Select all, Clear and the Build filter help with a large fleet.
  4. If the template has secret fields, type the values to set in Secrets. Leave a box empty to keep each device's current value.
  5. Click Preview. Read the pushes, the firmware verdicts and the secrets that will be set or kept.
  6. Click Deploy and confirm. Progress appears in the job dock.

Deploy is enabled only by a preview of the same selection. If you change a device, a secret or the limit box, preview again.

Configuration#

Nothing to configure. Which devices a Web Protection Profile template governs is chosen when it is approved, or here with Limit this template to the selected devices (see Advanced).

Example#

Change the SMTP server on every FortiWeb. FortiWeb keeps its mail settings in Log & Report → Email Policy (log/email-policy: SMTP server, port, authentication, user name, password, connection security, sender and recipients).

  1. On one device, open the email policy and click Save as template.
  2. In the Template Library, edit the SMTP server and have the template approved.
  3. In Mass Deploy, select it, select the devices and type the SMTP password.
  4. Preview, then deploy.

Result#

  • Every selected device runs the template's settings, and the secret you typed is set on each one.
  • Deploy history lists the deploy: when, who, the version, the devices, the result per device (with the device's error), the secret fields set (names only) and how many devices were bound.
  • The audit log has mass_deploy.preview, mass_deploy.start and the job's template.apply rows.

Troubleshooting#

Symptom Cause and fix
A device's box is greyed out It is bound to another version of the template (Not selectable: pinned to vN). Change its binding in the Template Library's View dialog.
Preview: the approval does not cover build X — revalidate the template for it The approval was not validated for that build. Revalidate it in the Template Library, or have an approver deploy with an override reason. Mass Deploy asks for this even for one device.
Preview: no value for … The device's binding leaves a {{ variable }} unset. Set it on the binding.
This template is not the newest approved version A newer version was approved since the page loaded. Reload and select it.
History: aborted, the canary's error The first device refused the write, so the rest were not run. The error is the device's own, for example HTTP 423 — errcode -20010 when the FortiWeb's licence is not valid.

Advanced#

Secrets are never pushed from a template. A secret field in a template body is empty, another device's ENC … ciphertext, or a plaintext value that should not sit in a database. So every push (Mass Deploy, the Template Library's Apply and the approval rollout) leaves it out and the device keeps its own value. What you type in Mass Deploy is used for that deploy only. It is not stored, logged or sent back in the preview, and the change history and the job record show <secret>.

Web Protection Profiles for some devices. A WPP template governs either every FortiWeb of the ADOM or only the devices bound to it:

  • When it governs only its bound devices, Mass Deploy binds each device it is deployed to. The profile becomes read-only there, and later approved versions are deployed to it.
  • When it governs every FortiWeb, the page offers Limit this template to the selected devices. Unchecked, the template is pushed and keeps governing all devices. Checked, the selected devices are bound and the template governs, locks and is deployed to bound devices only from then on.
  • To approve a special profile without it landing on every device, choose Only the devices I pick in Mass Deploy in the Template Library's approve dialog. Nothing is deployed or locked until Mass Deploy binds a device.

Pinned devices. A device whose binding pins another version of the family (or follows a newer one) is refused by Mass Deploy and by any fleet rollout from the Template Library. No override exists for this: the binding decides which version a device runs.
